content.title: Portland Fire select 3 players in 2026 WNBA Draft
content.text: PORTLAND Ore. (KPTV) - The Portland Fire hosted a watch party for fans at the Moda Center during the 2026 WNBA Draft on Monday.The Fire selected three players in the draft to expand their roster from the expansion draft and free agency signings.Portland selected Spanish guard Iyana Martín with the No. 7 overall pick. She was MVP of the 2023 FIBA U19 World Cup while representing her native company of Spain, and plays professionally for Perfumerías Avenida.Following the draft, Fire GM Vanja Černivec announced that Martín would remain overseas in 2026, and would join the Fire for the 2027 season.In the second round, Portland selected German forward Frieda Bühner No. 17 overall, who played professionally in Spain last season.Bühner played four games for the Florida Gators in the 2022-23 season.After initially selecting TCU guard Taylor Bigby, a former Oregon Duck, in the third round at No. 37 overall, the team traded the rights to Bigby and a future pick to the Connecticut Sun for the rights to the No. 33 pick, UConn forward Serah Williams.Williams spent three seasons at Wisconsin before finishing her career with the Huskies.Portland Fire GM Vanja Černivec speaks to the media after the 2026 WNBA Draft at Moda Center.(KPTV)Training camp is set for Sunday, ahead of the Fire’s first preseason game against the Seattle Storm on April 29.2026 WNBA Draft live blog:6:20 p.m. Portland Fire announced they had traded the No. 37 pick, TCU guard Taylor Bigby, and a 2027 pick to the Connecticut Sun for the No. 33 pick, UConn forward Serah Williams.5:50 p.m. Portland Fire select forward Frieda Bühner from Germany with their No. 17 pick.4:50 p.m. Portland Fire select guard Iyana Martín from Spain with the No. 7 pick.Copyright 2026 KPTV-KPDX.
